glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
itakumari-zamindar-bari.desc: Itakumari, in Pirgachha upazila, was the seat of Raja Raghunath Chandra Roy and his son Raja Shib Chandra Roy. In 1783 Shib Chandra helped lead the Rangpur peasants' rising against the tax farmer Debi Singh, alongside Debi Chaudhurani of nearby Manthana. The estate was once so known for learning that people called it a second Nabadwip. Today the house, a temple and a large pond survive in poor repair, with much of the old grandeur gone. It is a quiet place for anyone interested in the region's history.
blocks: How to get there
From Rangpur take a bus or CNG to Pirgachha, then an auto or van to Itakumari village.
Good to know
There is no ticket or guide; ask locals at the bazar to show you the house and temple. Be careful around crumbling walls.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
carmichael-college.desc: Founded in 1916 and named after Lord Carmichael, then Governor of Bengal, this is one of the oldest colleges in North Bengal. Its main academic building stretches in a long arcade with domes and arches, blending Mughal and colonial details. The campus covers a large area of fields, ponds and trees, popular with walkers in the evening. It has played an important role in the region's education and politics.
blocks: How to get there
On the eastern side of Rangpur city at Lalbagh; any rickshaw will take you.
Good to know
It is a working college, so be respectful during class hours.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
chikli-beel-park.desc: Chikli Beel is a century-old wetland in the Hanuman Tola area on the northern edge of Rangpur city. The City Corporation has turned its banks into a park, with walkways, benches, children's rides and boats on the water. In the evening a lit-up fountain draws crowds, and in winter migratory birds settle on the beel. It is the easiest green escape from the city centre for a couple of hours.
blocks: How to get there
A short rickshaw or auto ride from central Rangpur to Hanuman Tola; Rangpur Zoo is close by.
Good to know
Come late afternoon and stay for the evening fountain. Winter mornings are best for birds.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
Ticketed; small fee for locals, higher for foreigners (approx.)
tajhat-palace.desc: Built in the early 20th century by Maharaja Kumar Gopal Lal Roy, Tajhat Palace has a symmetrical facade topped by a central dome and wide flights of steps. Its interior staircase is made of Italian marble, and the building is set behind lawns, fountains and ponds. It now houses a museum displaying Sanskrit and Arabic manuscripts, terracotta, sculpture and other artefacts. For a time it also served as a bench of the High Court.
blocks: How to get there
About 3 km from Rangpur city centre; take a rickshaw or auto-rickshaw to Tajhat.
Good to know
Check the weekly closing day. Afternoon light on the white facade is lovely.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
nisbetganj-shotoronji.desc: Shotoronji is a flat-woven cotton rug made on a ground loom, without a shuttle, by passing coloured yarn by hand through the warp. The craft has a long history in Rangpur and centres on the village of Nisbetganj. Traditional designs are bold stripes and geometric patterns, now joined by modern colours for homes and export. Visitors can watch weavers at work and buy rugs, mats and wall hangings directly.
blocks: How to get there
Nisbetganj is a short auto-rickshaw ride from Rangpur city centre.
Good to know
Buying from the village workshops supports the weavers directly.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
begum-rokeya-memorial.desc: Begum Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain was born in 1880 in the village of Pairaband and became one of the most important voices for women's rights and education in Bengal. Her writings, including the feminist utopia 'Sultana's Dream', are still widely read. A memorial centre in the village holds a library and exhibits on her life, and the remains of her family home stand nearby. Her birthday, 9 December, is marked as Rokeya Day across Bangladesh.
blocks: How to get there
Pairaband is in Mithapukur upazila, south of Rangpur city; take a bus towards Mithapukur and an auto-rickshaw to the village.
Good to know
Visit around 9 December for commemorations, or on a quiet weekday.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
Ticketed entry (around 100 BDT per person; rides charged separately)
bhinno-jagat-park.desc: Bhinno Jagat lies at Gonjipur in Khaleya union, in the countryside north-west of Rangpur city. It is a large, green amusement park where families come for a full day out. There are the usual rides, from a Ferris wheel to a toy train, along with a small planetarium, a lake, prayer space and shops. The park also has its own rest houses and a community centre, so some visitors stay overnight. Weekends and Eid holidays get very crowded.
blocks: How to get there
From Rangpur city take a CNG or auto-rickshaw towards Khaleya/Gonjipur; drivers know the park by name.
Good to know
Go on a weekday morning to avoid the crowds. Carry cash for ride tickets.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
mithapukur-mosque.desc: Built around the early 19th century in the late Mughal style, the Mithapukur Mosque is a compact rectangular building topped by three domes with corner towers. Its facade carries decorative panels in plaster and brick. It sits in a village setting a short way from the Rangpur–Dhaka highway. Few travellers stop, which makes it a peaceful break on a road trip.
blocks: How to get there
In Mithapukur upazila, south of Rangpur; ask locally from Mithapukur bazar.
Good to know
Combine with Pairaband on the same trip. Dress modestly.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
Small ticket fee at the gate
rangpur-zoo.desc: Rangpur Zoo opened to visitors in 1991 on about 21 acres beside the Police Lines road, close to the district administration offices. It is the biggest zoo in the northern region. Among the animals are Bengal tigers, lions, a hippo, deer, monkeys, crocodiles and pythons, along with peacocks, parrots and other birds. Shady lawns, a children's park and an artificial lake make it a popular family outing.
blocks: How to get there
In Rangpur city, a rickshaw or auto to the zoo on the Police Lines–Hanuman Tola road.
Good to know
Morning visits are cooler and the animals are more active. Pair it with Chikli Beel nearby.

glance: 300 km to Rangpur by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
laldighi-nine-dome-mosque.desc: The mosque is named after the place, Laldighi, in Badarganj upazila, and is a protected archaeological site. It is thought to date from the late 17th or early 18th century; an inscription tablet that once sat on the east front has gone missing, so the exact year is unknown. Its nine domes and plan are similar to other mosques of that period. It was abandoned for a long time and was cleared of jungle and rediscovered during late British rule. Few outsiders come, so you will likely have it to yourself.
blocks: How to get there
From Rangpur take a bus to Badarganj or Taraganj; the mosque is about 5 km from Dholaighat bazar in Taraganj, reachable by CNG or easy-bike.
Good to know
Village roads can be muddy in the rains. Go outside prayer times and ask before entering.

glance: Shingara House at Jahaj Company Mor, beside Sri Sri Karunamoyi Kalibari, Rangpur city
rangpur-shingara-house.desc: Kanailal Sarkar opened Shingara House in Rangpur in 1960, and his family still runs it. The shop is cramped and plain, but there is nearly always a crowd for its small shingaras with a spiced potato filling, served with a thin sauce whose recipe the family keeps to itself. Generations of Rangpur people grew up on them. They are cheap enough to order a plateful.
blocks: Good to know
Eat them hot at the shop; they lose their crunch in a parcel.

glance: Homes and small rice hotels around Rangpur town and its villages; ask for it by name, as it is home food more than restaurant food
rangpur-sholka.desc: Sholka is one of the oldest home dishes of the Rangpur region. Jute leaves are simmered with other greens such as lau shak, kumro shak or napa shak in lightly salted water with green chilli, garlic and a little baking soda, which softens the leaves into a silky, loose soup. There is no oil, spice paste or onion; sometimes jackfruit seeds go in. It is eaten with rice at the start of a meal, the way other regions eat shukto or bitter greens.

glance: Home-style eateries and markets in Rangpur city; ask local families
rangpur-shidol.desc: Shidol is made by pounding dried small fish, usually puti, with taro stems and spices, shaping the paste into cakes and letting them cure. It is the classic preserved food of the northern districts, with a strong aroma that people from the region miss when they move away. The cakes are cooked into a fiery bhorta with garlic, onion and dried chilli, or into a thick curry. It is best eaten with hot rice in winter.
blocks: Good to know
The smell is strong but the taste is rich and savoury; try a small amount first.

glance: Roughly 60–150 BDT per kg in season
Mango markets in Mithapukur and Rangpur city during June–July
haribhanga-mango.desc: Haribhanga originated in Mithapukur upazila and has become Rangpur's pride. The fruit is round and heavy, with a small stone, smooth fibre-free flesh and a fragrant, sweet taste. Its popularity has grown quickly, and orchards now spread over much of the district. In season, traders and visitors crowd the markets around Mithapukur and Padagonj.
blocks: Good to know
The season peaks in late June to July, a little later than Rajshahi's early mangoes.
